title: VTP Modes & Versions
description: Configure VTP modes and understand how VTP server, client, and transparent behave.
scenario: Configure VTP modes and understand how VTP server, client, and transparent behave.

concepts.title: VTP Modes
concepts.body: VTP has three modes: Server (creates & advertises VLANs), Client (stores & learns, cannot create VLANs), Transparent (local VLANs only, forwards VTP messages).
concepts.code:
Server:     create VLANs, propagates
Client:     learns VLANs, no create
Transparent: local only, forwards

concepts.title: VTP Versions
concepts.body: VTPv1 is the original. VTPv2 adds support for Token Ring and better error handling. VTPv3 supports extended VLANs and password-security features. All switches in a domain should use the same version.
concepts.code:
Version 1: classic
Version 2: Token Ring support
Version 3: extended VLANs + security

concepts.title: VTP Domain & Revision
concepts.body: The domain name and revision number identify VTP messages. A higher revision number wins. Be careful — a switch with a high revision can wipe VLANs in the domain.
concepts.code:
SW1(config)# vtp domain CCNA
SW1(config)# vtp version 2
SW1(config)# vtp password cisco

concepts.title: Verifying VTP
concepts.body: "show vtp status" shows the mode and version on each switch. Verify all switches agree.
concepts.code:
SW1# show vtp status
VTP Version: 2
Domain Name: CCNA
VTP Mode: Server
Configuration Revision: 3
